findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, which assigns it a public DNS name and routable address, placing the database directly on the internet edge rather than behind the VPC boundary. Combined with the 'admin' master user and a password that is also written to EC2 user-data, this is a direct data-exfiltration path.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volumes, automated snapshots and backups, so all catalog/employee data is stored in cleartext at the storage layer.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web server. Any compromise of the PHP application yields full control of every bucket, instance and database in the account, including ec2:CreateTags/RunInstances-style privilege escalation and rds:ModifyDBInstance to reset the DB master password.

The RDS master username and the value of var.password are interpolated into the instance user_data script and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user-data is stored unencrypted and is readable by anyone who can reach the instance metadata service (e.g. via SSRF in the PHP app) or who holds ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the database master credentials.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 (token-less) remains enabled. Because the instance profile carries s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* on all resources, a single SSRF or request-forgery bug in the PHP page exposed on this host is enough to retrieve near-administrative role credentials.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block sets encrypted = true, so the volume holding the credential file /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc is written to unencrypted storage and any snapshot of it inherits that exposure.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the form over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration or listener. Employee name/address submissions and any session data traverse the network in cleartext, and the output of the instance public DNS confirms the host is intended to be reached externally.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1. The application connects with mysqli_connect without any TLS options, so database traffic including the master credentials can traverse the network unencrypted.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised database host has an unconstrained outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control; egress from a data tier should be tightly scoped.

The master username is hard-coded to the well-known default 'admin', which removes any guessing effort for credential-stuffing or brute-force attempts against an instance that is also publicly accessible.

The master password is supplied from var.password and reused verbatim in instance user-data rather than being generated and stored in Secrets Manager or SSM SecureString. The value is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state and is likely to appear in plan output or version control.

iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so the deployment relies solely on a static shared master password that is distributed to the application host, rather than short-lived IAM-issued tokens.
